applicableAreas: biofiltration/detention pond area in northeast portion of site
southern property boundary where overhead electric line is located
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows overhead electric line (OHE) running along the southern property boundary. Sheet 15 and 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan and Profiles) show the biofiltration/detention pond located in the northeast portion of the site. However, the site plan contains no dimension lines, distance callouts, or clearance calculations between the pond water surface and the overhead electric conductors. The pond profile sheets (Sheet 16) show cross-sectional views of the pond with water surface elevations (100-yr: 676.75 ft, 25-yr: 676.57 ft, etc.) but contain no depiction of overhead electric facilities or clearance measurements. No engineer-sealed profile or section exhibits verify that the required 7.5 feet horizontal (sky-to-ground) clearance from overhead distribution conductors is maintained.
findings.reasoning: The regulatory requirement (UCM § 1.10.3) mandates that water quality features maintain a minimum 7.5-foot horizontal sky-to-ground clearance from the outermost conductor of overhead distribution lines. While overhead electric lines are present on the site (visible on Sheet 9), no clearance verification, dimensions, or professional engineer certification is provided on the site plan, drainage plan, or profile sheets. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant; the absence of clearance documentation or calculations prevents confirmation that this requirement is met. This constitutes insufficient documentation rather than definitive non-compliance, warranting an 'unclear' status pending clarification.
findings.comment: Overhead distribution conductors are present on the southern property boundary, but water quality feature clearance distances are not documented. Provide engineer-sealed profile or section views demonstrating that the biofiltration/detention pond maintains a minimum 7.5 feet horizontal (sky-to-ground) clearance from the outermost overhead distribution primary, neutral, or secondary conductors.

applicableAreas: biofiltration/detention pond area in northeast portion of site
findings.observation: Site plan shows overhead electric line on southern boundary. Drainage and biofiltration pond sheets show pond location in northeast area with no radial clearance measurements or documentation. No profile, section, or plan view indicates distances from the pond boundary to any overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors in any direction (radial). No callouts, dimensions, or engineer certification verify the required 15-foot radial clearance in all directions from the pond perimeter.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 requires a minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors to the water quality feature boundary, measured in all directions from the conductors. The site plan provides no measurements, calculations, or professional certification of this radial clearance. The applicant bears the burden of demonstrating compliance; the complete absence of radial clearance documentation prevents verification that this requirement is satisfied.
findings.comment: No radial clearance verification is documented between the biofiltration/detention pond and overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors. Provide engineer-sealed plan and profile views with scaled measurements and callouts demonstrating that the pond maintains a minimum 15-foot radial clearance from overhead distribution primary and neutral conductors in all directions.

applicableAreas: underground electric equipment locations throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) identifies multiple underground electrical transformer pads and pull boxes distributed throughout the site. Sheet 15 shows biofiltration-detention pond plan with detailed elevations and infrastructure. However, no dimension lines, distance measurements, or clearance calculations connect the pond boundaries to any underground electrical equipment locations. No cross-section or profile view shows the vertical or horizontal relationship between the pond and nearby transformer pads or pull boxes. The Electrical Design Plan and Drainage Plan sheets do not coordinate to verify clearance distances between water quality features and underground distribution equipment.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.7 requires water quality features to maintain a minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from underground distribution equipment such as transformers and pull boxes. While underground electrical equipment is present on the site (transformers, pull boxes documented on Sheet 21) and a water quality pond is present (Sheet 15), no measurements or clearance verification are provided. The applicant has not documented that the required clearance is maintained. The absence of this documentation prevents verification of compliance.
findings.comment: Underground electrical transformers and pull boxes are located throughout the site, and a biofiltration/detention pond is proposed, but clearance distances are not documented. Provide plan and profile views with dimensions and callouts demonstrating that the water quality feature maintains a minimum 10-foot horizontal clearance from all underground distribution equipment (transformers, pull boxes, vaults).

applicableAreas: underground electric line routing throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Electrical Design Plan) shows underground electric lines (depicted as blue lines) routing throughout the site with multiple connections to transformers, pull boxes, and building meters. Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan) shows the pond location and construction details. However, no cross-references, clearance calculations, or dimension lines on either sheet verify the distance between the pond boundaries and the underground electric conduit/conductor routing. No profile or cross-section demonstrates the vertical separation or horizontal distance from the pond to underground electric lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.7 requires water quality features to maintain a minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from underground electric conduits and conductors. Underground electric lines are clearly present on the site routing near the pond area, but no clearance documentation or measurements verify that the required 5-foot minimum distance is maintained. The absence of this coordination and documentation prevents confirmation of compliance.
findings.comment: Underground electric lines are routed throughout the site in proximity to the biofiltration/detention pond, but clearance distances are not documented. Provide plan and profile views with dimensions and professional engineer certification demonstrating that the water quality feature maintains a minimum 5-foot horizontal clearance from all underground electric conduits and conductors.

applicableAreas: biofiltration-detention pond area and water quality features
southern property boundary where overhead electric line is located
findings.observation: Sheet 15 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Plan & Calculations) and Sheet 16 (Biofiltration-Detention Pond Profiles) present detailed engineering information for the pond system. Sheet 16 contains cross-sectional profiles ('Pond Section A-A', 'Pond Section B-B', and 'Pond Outfall Detail') showing pond infrastructure, retaining walls, pipe routing, and elevation data. However, examination of these profile sheets reveals: (1) No overhead electric lines, conductors, or poles are depicted in any section view; (2) No clearance dimensions, measurements, or distance callouts between the pond and electric facilities are shown; (3) No professional engineer seal or notation indicating clearance verification for electric conductors; (4) The standard utility disclaimer note at the bottom states utilities 'may not match locations as constructed' but provides no affirmative clearance verification. The profiles show only pond construction details without reference to or coordination with the overhead electric line shown on Sheet 9 (Site Plan).
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.3 explicitly requires profile plans and engineer-sealed section exhibits showing clearance verification between water quality features and all phases of overhead electric conductors and poles. The deficiency definition specifies 'missing required profile plans, engineer-scaled section exhibits, or elevation views showing clearance verification and dimensions.' The pond profile sheets on Sheet 16 contain no overhead electric conductors or clearance dimensions—these sheets address only stormwater construction details. The regulatory requirement mandates that such clearance documentation exist and be provided; its complete absence constitutes a clear deficiency. The engineer must provide professionally-sealed profile or section views that explicitly depict the overhead electric facilities and demonstrate through dimensions and calculations that required clearances are maintained.
findings.comment: Profile sheets for the biofiltration-detention pond do not show or reference overhead electric conductors or clearance dimensions. Provide professionally engineer-sealed profile or section views depicting all overhead electric conductors and demonstrating clearance dimensions and calculations per UCM § 1.10.3 (minimum 7.5 feet horizontal sky-to-ground clearance, minimum 15 feet radial clearance from distribution primary and neutral conductors).

findings.observation: Sheet 2 (Plat) and Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depict 5' electric easements along the southern boundary ('5' Elec. & Tele. Easement Vol. 5468, Pg. 883 D.R.T.C.Tx.') and eastern boundary ('5' Electric Easement Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.'). On Sheet 9, multiple improvements are drawn directly overlapping or encroaching into these easement boundaries: (1) A Type III Driveway with notation 'Construct Type III Driveway See Detail 1/335-2' crosses completely through the southern 5' electric easement; (2) A 6' Concrete Sidewalk labeled 'Construct 6' Concrete Sidewalk See Dtl 4/335-1' crosses through the southern 5' easement; (3) Concrete Retaining Wall lines with notation 'Begin Concrete Retaining Wall at Existing Concrete Retaining Wall Tie to Existing Concrete Retaining Wall' overlap and encroach into both the southern and eastern 5' easement areas, running parallel to the easement boundaries. These structures are drawn directly on or overlapping the dashed easement boundary lines.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 explicitly prohibits permanent structures, buildings, overhangs, balconies, canopies, stairways, eaves, awnings, patios, roofed structures, and permanent improvements (including below-grade footings) within electric easements. Driveways, sidewalks, and retaining walls are permanent improvements. The site plan clearly depicts these improvements overlapping the drawn easement boundary lines. The graphic evidence from Sheet 9 shows these structures encroaching into the dedicated easement areas. UCM § 1.10.10.2 is absolute: 'no structures are permitted above or below grade' within electric easements; the site plan violates this prohibition.
findings.comment: Concrete retaining walls, Type III driveway, and concrete sidewalk are shown encroaching into the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all structures and permanent improvements outside the electric easement boundaries, or provide evidence that these easements have been abandoned or modified. Coordinate with Austin Energy to verify easement status.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts multiple tree and vegetation symbols (circles with branching patterns indicating trees) directly within the southern 5' electric easement along the southern property line and within the eastern 5' electric easement along the eastern property line. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) confirms tree placement with symbols labeled 'M' (Mitigation Trees), 'PL' (Parking Lot Trees), and 'P' (Parking Buffer Point Trees) positioned adjacent to or within these easement areas. The Landscape Plan contains 'IRRIGATION NOTES' but does not reference any license agreement from Austin Energy. The site plan notes on Sheet 3 contain no statement confirming that a license agreement has been 'obtained from and filed with' Austin Energy Public Involvement. Site plan notes use general language about easement provision but do not specifically confirm an executed license agreement for landscaping/irrigation within the electric easements.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 is explicit and unambiguous: 'Landscaping and irrigation systems [are] permissible within easements only with license agreement obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement.' The regulatory standard uses the exact phrase 'obtained from and filed with'—not 'to be obtained' and not 'requested.' The site plan shows landscaping (trees) within easement boundaries but provides no documentation of an executed license agreement. The burden of demonstrating compliance is on the applicant. Missing executed license agreement documentation is grounds for deficiency, as this can result in certificate of occupancy holds and Austin Energy removal of non-compliant landscaping at the owner's cost.
findings.comment: Trees and vegetation are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas without documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy Public Involvement. Provide a copy of the executed license agreement 'obtained from and filed with Austin Energy Public Involvement' authorizing landscaping and irrigation within these easements, or relocate all landscaping outside the easement boundaries.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts concrete retaining walls, a wood fence, driveways, and sidewalks located within or directly overlapping the southern and eastern 5' electric easement boundaries. These physical structures create barriers and obstructions to the easement area. Retaining walls run parallel to easement boundaries at the perimeter, creating access restrictions. The wood fence is drawn directly within the eastern 5' easement area. Driveways and sidewalks, while potentially providing some access routes, are designed for pedestrian and vehicle traffic to/from buildings rather than maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. No dimensions or callout indicate that a clear, continuous, drivable maintenance corridor is maintained within or adjacent to these easements. The plan shows landscaping (trees) also positioned within easement areas, further reducing open access.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.3 states that landscaping within easements is permitted only 'if landscaping does not restrict 24/7 access.' The phrase is also reinforced in the general prohibition language emphasizing that Austin Energy must maintain '24-hour unimpeded access to all electric facilities.' Retaining walls and fences are structures that inherently restrict access; trees and vegetation also impede equipment movement. The site plan shows these features within the easement boundaries, and there is no notation, callout, or specification stating that a 24/7 maintenance access corridor is maintained free of obstruction. The presence of these features within the easement area violates the requirement for unrestricted access.
findings.comment: Retaining walls, fences, landscaping, and other improvements within the electric easements obstruct required 24/7 vehicular maintenance access for Austin Energy personnel and equipment. Ensure that easement areas remain completely clear of all obstructions and maintain a continuous, unobstructed access corridor at least 12 feet wide within the easement for Austin Energy maintenance activities.

applicableAreas: eastern 5' electric easement area near southeast portion of site
findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) depicts a line labeled 'Wood Fence' running along the property boundary directly within the eastern 5' Electric Easement area (Vol. 69, Pg. 14; Vol. 73, Pg. 76 P.R.T.C.Tx.). The site plan detail references and notes indicate this is a wooden privacy fence as part of the landscaping/site amenity design ('wooden privacy fence' notations visible in landscape and site plan details). A wooden privacy fence is a permanent structure designed to remain in place; it is not removable. The fence is located between Building 6 and the eastern property boundary, directly overlapping the dashed easement line.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 contains an exception: 'Removable wooden fences may be allowed in easements under license agreement if removable to permit Austin Energy crew and equipment access.' However, the prohibition is clear for permanent or masonry fencing. The site plan shows a 'privacy fence,' which by nature and nomenclature is a permanent landscape feature not designed for removal. There is no notation stating the fence is removable or that a license agreement allows its installation. The fence is depicted as a permanent improvement within the easement area, directly violating UCM § 1.10.10.2.
findings.comment: A permanent wood privacy fence is shown within the eastern 5' electric easement. Remove the fence from the easement, or if a removable wooden fence is intended, provide documentation of a license agreement from Austin Energy and specifications clearly identifying the fence as removable to permit Austin Energy maintenance access.

findings.observation: Sheet 9 (Site Plan) shows multiple tree symbols (circles with branching canopy patterns) drawn directly on or overlapping the dashed lines indicating the southern 5' electric easement and eastern 5' electric easement. Sheet 31 (Landscape Plan) further documents these tree placements with legend symbols 'M' (Mitigation Tree), 'PL' (Parking Lot Tree), and 'P' (Parking Buffer Point Tree) positioned in these same easement areas along the southern and eastern property boundaries. Trees are site amenities and landscape features. The vision analysis of Sheet 9 confirmed: 'Multiple tree symbols (circles with branching patterns) are drawn directly on top of and within the dashed boundaries of this easement along the southern property line. Tree and vegetation symbols are drawn between the eastern property line and 'Bldg. 6', sitting directly within the marked 5' easement space.'
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 prohibits structures within electric easements where 'only electric facilities are permitted ground to sky.' Trees are structures with above-ground canopies and below-grade root systems. Site amenities, including landscaping features such as trees, are explicitly prohibited in the code. The site plan depicts multiple trees directly within the southernnortheastern 5' easement areas, violating this prohibition. Trees also trigger irrigation requirements (landscaping cannot survive without water in the arid Austin climate), which then implicates tree maintenance access, fertilization, and potential pruning—all activities that would further obstruct Austin Energy's access rights.
findings.comment: Multiple trees and vegetation (site amenities) are shown within the southern and eastern 5' electric easement areas. Relocate all trees and landscaping outside the electric easement boundaries to comply with UCM § 1.10.10.2.

applicableAreas: electrical vault easement area west of Building 8
multiple electrical pull box locations throughout site
findings.observation: Sheet 21 (Preliminary Electrical Design Plan) identifies a 'Vault Easement' on the west side of Building 8, with an adjacent 'Electrical Pull Box.' Multiple 'Electrical Pull Box' locations are marked throughout the site (north of Bldg. 1, north of Bldg. 3, northeast of Bldg. 4, west of Bldg. 2, central corridor, east of Bldg. 6, and others). However, no dimensions, clearance measurements, or distance callouts on Sheet 21 verify that structures, landscaping, or improvements maintain the required minimum 8-foot clearance around these pedestals, subsurface vaults, or equipment access points in all directions. The electrical plan shows building footprints, driveways, and other site features in proximity to these equipment locations but provides no specific distance verification or engineer notation confirming 8-foot clearances.
findings.reasoning: UCM § 1.10.10.2 requires 'minimum 8-foot clearance around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, or manholes requiring personnel access.' This is a quantified, measurable requirement. The site plan identifies multiple electrical vaults and pull boxes but provides no measurements or callouts demonstrating that the required 8-foot clearance is maintained around these facilities in all directions. While the clearance may in fact be maintained, the applicant has not provided documentation or certification of this compliance. The burden is on the applicant to affirmatively demonstrate that the requirement is met; the absence of this documentation prevents verification.
findings.comment: Electrical vaults, pedestals, and pull boxes are located throughout the site, but 8-foot clearances are not documented with dimensions or callouts. Provide plan views with dimensions and professional engineer certification verifying that a minimum 8-foot clearance in all directions is maintained around all pedestals, subsurface vaults, and electrical equipment requiring personnel access.
